chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Performing by feeling; the song Belittlin' Me
summary: He taught himself how to sell to an audience by feel and explains he wrote Belittlin' Me to counter heckling.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: The thing that also amazes me about you as a performer is that you seem to have an intuitive sense for what pleased an audience, how to sell what you were doing to an audience.
That's the thing that's necessary. That's more necessary than
But nobody taught it to you.
Well, I felt it. I felt it.
So your performing was very much on a feeling level then.

That's right. Just like the song I wrote called, 'Belittlin' Me.' See I felt that a song was necessary to keep these people from heckling. But they could say, Hello George or Jim or Henry to any old body and be all right. So that's why I wrote that song.
There's another song that's terrific. However --
